comments.text: For some reason, everyone who talks about Siberia mentions the Trans-Siberian Railway—a massive undertaking. Yet, I’ve never heard anyone mention another major railway project that spans the entirety of Siberia: the BAM (Baikal-Amur Mainline). It was even more ambitious than the Trans-Siberian Railway. While the original Trans-Siberian Railway was single-track (meaning trains could only move in one direction), the Soviet Union built the BAM as a double-track line—also stretching across all of Siberia—and subsequently upgraded the Trans-Siberian Railway by adding a second track. Please look into the BAM and create a dedicated video about it; there is very little information available on this subject in English.

comments.author: @PotatoRadius
comments.text:
10:22 The map contains several errors concerning Finland.

(1) It shows Finland as a part of Russia, but in fact, the country gained its independence from Russia at the end of 1917.

I suppose the map could be said to be accurate up to December 1917, if it wasn't for:

(2) The whole country is coloured red. While there was a civil war in Finland in the first half of 1918 with a Red side and a White side, at no point did the whole country come under Red control. Also, it was a separate war, so shouldn't be conflated with the Russian civil war.

(3) The map shows Finland as having a northeastern extension that reaches the Arctic Ocean. This was the case in 1920–44, that is, after the country became independent.
